skill.name: penetration-testing-with-strix
skill.description: Pentest a web app, API, codebase, repository, URL, domain, or IP with Strix — autonomous AI penetration testing that exploits and proves vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10 and beyond — injection, XSS, SSRF, auth/access-control flaws, IDOR, business logic) instead of just flagging them. Runs self-hosted with the open-source CLI or via the managed app.strix.ai cloud, and returns validated findings with proof-of-concept exploits (Markdown, JSON, CSV, SARIF). Use when the user asks to pentest, hack, security-scan, security-audit, or find vulnerabilities in an app, API, website, or repo.
skill.summary: Guide authorized Strix penetration tests through local or cloud workflows, with scoped scans, spending limits, and evidence-based reporting.
skill.author: usestrix

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown, documentation URLs, example targets, or placeholder configuration, not executable backticks or leaked secrets. The installer executes unverified remote code, while prose also risks credential exposure and misleading privacy expectations. No evidence found of prompt injection or deliberate credential exfiltration in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: The installation command pipes a mutable remote script directly into Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Require installation approval and replace direct piping with a pinned release whose signature or checksum is verified before execution.

remediation.issue: The authentication example places credentials directly in a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use the documented instruction-file option with restrictive permissions and redacted logging; use dedicated test accounts and remove temporary files afterward.

remediation.issue: The self-hosted workflow claims full locality while showing a hosted model provider.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that hosted LLMs may receive analyzed content; require an approved local model and verified network isolation for offline or source-confidential testing.

content.user_title: Run Authorized Penetration Tests with Strix
content.value_statement: Application security teams need reproducible testing with clear scope, costs, and evidence. This skill guides Strix setup, authorized scans, and interpretation of validated findings.
actual_capabilities: Guide selection between self-hosted Docker scans and managed Strix cloud testing.
Compose headless scan commands for repositories, deployed applications, API specifications, and target lists.
Explain scan modes, budget caps, turn limits, diff scope, and severity-based exit thresholds.
Guide cloud login, domain registration, ownership verification, scan execution, and finding retrieval.
Locate Markdown, JSON, CSV, and SARIF artifacts and summarize proof-of-concept evidence by severity.
Interpret exit codes and identify coverage limitations caused by budget or turn limits.
limitations: This skill contains instructions only; testing requires an installed Strix CLI or access to its managed service.
Self-hosted scans require Docker and a configured model; hosted model providers can receive analyzed content.
Testing can exploit applications and modify writable repository targets; authorization and disposable checkouts are required.
A clean exit does not prove complete coverage; budget limits, cloud credits, and service access can constrain testing.

best_practices: Confirm target authorization, exclusions, and explicit approval for cloud source uploads before scanning.
Verify installation artifacts, use disposable checkouts, and keep credentials out of command arguments and shared logs.
Set spending limits and review evidence, run status, cost, and coverage before accepting results.
anti_patterns: Scanning third-party systems without documented permission or treating domain reachability as authorization.
Executing unverified remote installers or exposing valuable uncommitted work through writable mounts.
Assuming self-hosted means offline or treating exit code zero as proof that all targets are secure.

faq.question: Does the skill include the Strix scanning engine?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions for the separately installed Strix CLI and managed service.

faq.question: Do I need Docker?
faq.answer: Self-hosted testing requires Docker. Managed cloud testing does not require local Docker, but needs service access and target verification.

faq.question: Can I test any public website?
faq.answer: No. Only test systems you own or have explicit authorization to assess.

faq.question: Does self-hosted testing keep source code local?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Hosted model providers can receive analyzed content. Confidential or offline testing requires an approved local model and verified network controls.

faq.question: How are testing costs controlled?
faq.answer: The CLI supports budget and turn limits. Managed testing uses service credits. Limits can stop testing before coverage is complete.

faq.question: Does a successful exit mean the application is secure?
faq.answer: No. Review report evidence, run status, spending, and coverage. Budget warnings or limits can leave testing incomplete despite a successful exit.
